methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort of 217 patients with stratification by first-line treatment (CT+IO n=82, CT alone n=32, targeted therapy n=16, supportive care n=87). As-treated analysis performed. Authors explicitly acknowledge baseline imbalances between CT+IO and CT-alone groups including sex distribution, histology, ECOG performance status, brain metastases, and chemotherapy backbone that confound survival comparisons. Cox proportional hazards regression applied with univariate screening (p<0.1) and multivariate model (p<0.05). Sensitivity analysis excluding missing ECOG PS performed. CT-alone cohort notably small (n=32) limiting statistical power; 24.4% missing ECOG PS data across cohort.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study comparing treatment strategies with survival outcomes (LoE 2b). Addresses clinically relevant question regarding real-world effectiveness of CT+IO in understudied PD-L1 <1% NSCLC population, where trial evidence shows modest benefit (13-17 months OS). Real-world OS slightly shorter (14.4 months CT+IO vs 13.5 CT alone) but underpowered to demonstrate significant difference. Study highlights practice pattern variability and patient selection factors not captured in trials.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational study with STROBE-aligned reporting: patient flow documented (Figure 1), baseline characteristics comprehensively presented (Table 1), treatment patterns detailed (Tables 2-3, Figure 1), survival outcomes with Kaplan-Meier curves and stratified subgroup analyses (Figures 2-4), adverse events systematically collected (Table 5). However, extensive missing data (24.4% ECOG PS, undocumented reasons for treatment decisions in some cases) impacts completeness. Heterogeneous progression assessment via clinical documentation rather than standardized RECIST criteria acknowledged. Data availability: no explicit statement regarding data repository access.

novelty_literature.justification: Real-world evidence study filling documented gap in literature regarding CT+IO comparative effectiveness in PD-L1 <1% NSCLC—an understudied population with unclear trial-to-practice translation. Contributes practice pattern documentation and highlights discrepancies between trial inclusion criteria and real-world patient populations. However, retrospective observational design without novel methodology or mechanistic insights; lacks external validation cohort.

writing_presentation.justification: Excellently organized real-world evidence paper with clear clinical context establishing PD-L1 <1% NSCLC as understudied population with modest trial benefits. Transparent discussion of why clinical trial results may not translate to practice, including selection bias, heterogeneous imaging assessment, incomplete documentation, and missing clinical factors. Comprehensive limitations section acknowledging small CT-alone sample, baseline imbalances, missing data, single-center referral bias, and non-randomized design. Publication-ready clarity and structure.

key_strengths: Addresses clinically important real-world evidence gap in understudied PD-L1 <1% NSCLC population where trial benefits are modest and practice patterns poorly characterized

Comprehensive documentation of treatment selection rationale and reasons for non-treatment (33.3% poor PS, 24.4% patient decision, 19.3% physician-deemed ineligible), revealing disconnect between trial and real-world patient selection

Transparent acknowledgment of methodological constraints including 24.4% missing ECOG PS, baseline imbalances between treatment groups (sex, histology, ECOG, brain metastases), heterogeneous imaging intervals, and selection bias inherent to retrospective design
Toxicity profile (53.7% clinically significant TRAE in CT+IO, 29.3% irAEs, 8.5% pneumonitis) consistent with clinical trials, supporting safety evidence in broader population than trial participants
key_concerns: Small and imbalanced CT-alone comparator cohort (n=32) with higher proportion of ECOG PS 2, squamous histology, and lower brain metastases; insufficient power to detect meaningful survival differences; null OS/PFS findings lack statistical power for definitive conclusion

Extensive missing data (24.4% ECOG PS) impacting treatment allocation bias assessment; heterogeneous progression ascertainment via clinical notes and variable imaging intervals rather than standardized RECIST, introducing potential assessment bias in PFS determination

Baseline imbalances (sex: 56.1% vs 71.9% male, squamous: 19.5% vs 37.5%, ECOG 2: 9.8% vs 18.8%, brain metastases: 15.9% vs 6.3%) confound treatment efficacy comparisons; multivariate adjustment limited by small CT-alone sample and missing data

Single-center academic setting with potential referral bias; results may not generalize to community oncology practices or diverse geographic populations; conclusion regarding real-world CT+IO lack of benefit underpowered and hypothesis-generating at best
chief_reviewer.rationale: Pragmatic real-world evidence study addressing clinically relevant gap in PD-L1 negative NSCLC literature, but small imbalanced comparator cohort, extensive missing data, and non-randomized design with baseline confounding limit tier placement to 4. Appropriate for specialty journals reporting real-world outcomes with clear caveats on power and generalizability.
